input.quote: 13.5 Liquidated Damages. Customer acknowledges that M&I shall suffer a material adverse impact on its business if this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A) and that the resulting damages may not be susceptible of precise determination. Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
input.rationale:
Section 13.5 expressly creates liquidated damages payable by Customer (not by M&I), deeming the Termination for Convenience Fee and Termination for Cause Fee to be liquidated damages and not a penalty. Those fees are measured as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value (p0039 — remaining months multiplied by the greater of the Monthly Base Fee or average monthly Fees) and are expressly carved out of the Section 13.4 liability cap, so the deemed liquidated amount tracks the remaining contract value rather than the three months' fees permitted by the fallback. That fails the fallback and approaches walk-away territory. The smallest edit to reach the preferred position is deletion of the deeming provision; the quantum of the termination fees themselves is addressed under the termination-for-convenience rule and is not re-flagged here. Section 11.2(B) (p0190) correctly confirms no fees are payable where Customer terminates for M&I's default.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.85

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted Section 13.5 because our playbook does not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and deeming a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value to be liquidated damages measures M&I's recovery by the remaining contract value rather than its actual loss. If a termination fee is unavoidable, we can accept one capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
proposal.summary: Delete the liquidated damages deeming provision in Section 13.5.
